title: The Focal Point
hook: If customers have to guess where to go next, a bunch of them will guess wrong.
statement: When people can't talk it through, they land on whatever choice feels obvious to everyone.
explainer: People coordinate around what stands out, not what's most logical. Make your default option the obvious one and people find it without being told.
sop: Find a moment where people must coordinate with you without asking.
List every option they might pick.
Rate the Focal Salience of your preferred option from 1 to 10.
Make it more prominent with naming, placement, and repetition.
Remove competing options that split attention.
equation_example: Your default meeting spot scores a Focal Salience of 9, so people show up there almost automatically. Score a 3 and everyone scatters and has to sort it out. Higher means people line up without a word. Lower means every handoff needs explaining.
question: Pick one place customers get confused about next steps and make one option obvious.
closing_statement: Make the right choice the obvious one.
caption:
Principle Nº 344: The Focal Point

If customers have to guess where to go next, a bunch of them will guess wrong.

When people can't talk it through, they land on whatever choice feels obvious to everyone.

Your turn: Pick one place customers get confused about next steps and make one option obvious.
